notes: A caller that wraps a substrate read in `.catch(() => null)` or a try/catch — to turn a failure into an honest `unknown`/`unreadable` state, as `loadTrack2ProgrammeState` and `resolveTrack2Population` both already did, in already-merged, already-tested code — has a documented, load-bearing expectation that the wrapped function actually rejects on failure. A reader that instead catches its OWN error internally and resolves to an empty-but-valid result (`if (error) return [];`) defeats that expectation SILENTLY: the caller's catch never fires, the caller's own correctness is untouched by any test that mocks the reader directly (as this codebase's own test suite already did, correctly, for `loadTrack2ProgrammeState`), and the gap is invisible until a real query error occurs against the real function in production.

This is deliberately narrower than 'never swallow an error' — a function MAY legitimately choose fail-soft-to-empty as its OWN contract (this codebase already has that pattern elsewhere, e.g. call sites that write their own `.catch(() => [])`). The invariant is about a MISMATCH: a producer's swallow-to-success behaviour contradicting a consumer's already-written, already-relied-upon expectation that failure propagates. The fix is always to make the PRODUCER honest (throw), never to teach every consumer to route around a producer that lies about its own failures.

Two occurrences of the identical shape, in two different modules read by two different capabilities (Corpus Scout's `listCandidateSources` and Invariant Discovery's `listCandidates`), both discovered and fixed together on 2026-09-01 — the second was found by grepping for the same `if (error) return [];` pattern once the first was understood, not independently.

canaries.assertion: `listCandidateSources` and `listCandidates` each reject their returned promise when the underlying Supabase query reports an `error` — they must never resolve to `[]` on a genuine read failure. Both tests were verified failing against the pre-fix `if (error) return [];` bodies before the fix landed.

'an unreadable signal is NAMED, so a zero is not mistaken for a fact' — already asserts that a rejected `listCandidateSources` call surfaces as `populationUnreadable` containing 'corpus_candidate_sources', never as a false zero treated as fact. This test already existed and already passed (it mocks the function directly), which is exactly why the defect was invisible to the existing suite: the mock always behaved as the fix now makes the real function behave.

statement: A shared substrate-read function must not itself swallow a query error into an empty-but-successful result when any of its callers already depends — via `.catch()`, try/catch, or documented contract — on that failure propagating as a rejection. Make the producer honest; never route consumers around a producer that lies about its own failures.

occurrences.defect: `if (error) return [];` silently converted a genuine `corpus_candidate_sources` query failure (observed live: recurring Postgres statement timeouts) into a confidently-empty corpus. Defeated `researchProgrammeOrchestrator.ts`'s `.catch(() => null)` (documented fail-soft-to-`unknown` contract) and `track2Population.ts`'s own try/catch (documented fail-soft-to-`unreadable` contract) — both already written, both already correct, neither ever actually reachable. Produced the live EXP-P1 Track 2 oscillation: a stable, DB-confirmed corpus of 34 admitted + 18 pending sources intermittently rendered as '0 discovered, 0 admitted — Discover Sources not started', cascading through `unblockedStageIds` to strip the genuinely pending 'Review & Admit' human decision from `firstPendingDecision` entirely.

The identical `if (error) return [];` pattern over `discovery_candidates`, discovered by inspection once the first occurrence was understood — not yet observed to have fired in production, but read through the exact same `.catch(() => null)` contract in `loadTrack2ProgrammeState` and therefore capable of producing the identical class of false-empty read for Stage 3/4 (Extract Candidates / Review & Promote).
